speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to narrow down the cause, please describe exactly where the pain is located, how severe it is on a scale of 1 to 10, and if you have noticed any fever or chills.

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your history of recurrent urinary tract infections and current symptoms, have you experienced any recent episodes of fever, chills, or nausea? Additionally, have you noticed any passing of kidney stones or blood clots in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis).

While your history of recurrent UTIs is noted, the combination of visible hematuria and right flank pain is most classically indicative of a kidney stone. I will proceed to request a Urinalysis and a Non-Contrast CT of the Abdomen and Pelvis to confirm the presence of a stone and rule out other causes like an abscess or tumor.
